description.value: The study used fMRI to examine how sensory modality, object category, smoking status, and nicotine-dependence severity influence neural cue reactivity.

spans.text: In the present experiment, we employed functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to address these issues in the context of smoking.

description.value: A cross-sectional study of smokers and nonsmokers using a within-subject visual-versus-haptic cue-reactivity paradigm.

spans.text: The “smoking paraphernalia” and “control objects” conditions were presented either in the visual or haptic modality.

spans.text: Closing and reopening of the participant's grasping hand was cued by color changes of a centrally presented fixation cross
smoking paraphernalia

description.value: Participants were presented with four smoking-related objects—a cigarette, an ashtray, a normal cigarette box, and a longer cigarette box—or grayscale images of these objects. In the haptic condition they actively touched each object with the presented hand; in the visual condition they viewed the image without tactile stimulation. They followed the hand-closing and hand-reopening cues during each presentation.

spans.text: control objects

description.value: Participants were presented with four everyday control objects—a pen, a crème jar, a small video cassette, and an audio cassette—or grayscale images of these objects. In the haptic condition they actively touched each object with the presented hand; in the visual condition they viewed the image without tactile stimulation. They followed the hand-closing and hand-reopening cues during each presentation.

instructions.value: Participants closed and reopened their hand in response to color changes of a central fixation cross. They followed these instructions in every condition. In visual conditions they viewed grayscale images of objects; in haptic conditions they actively touched objects presented in the hand by the experimenter. During behavioral ratings, they rated how strong their urge to smoke was on a 1-to-10 scale and rated valence and arousal using the Self-Assessment Manikin.
